proposal.text: Q1: The default is set at src/hub.ts:65 (`static DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000)`), applied per room at hub.ts:94, with a duplicated legacy fallback at src/hub/persistence.ts:77. Verdict: KEEP 3 minutes for a nine-seat working session. (a) Silence nudge (hub.ts:1036-1060): re-armed on every post (hub.ts:985), so in a nine-seat room it fires only on genuine whole-room silence, and an identical nudge is posted at most twice (hub.ts:1055). More seats make it fire less often, not more. (b) Openings deadline (hub.ts:1081, 1093-1110; 6 min zero-openings at hub.ts:136): starts at the first opening and chat does not reset it. This is the tight case for nine staggered seats, but a late seat can still speak in chat, and unarrived seats get a warning plus one more period (hub.ts:1101-1104). Holding eight seats for one straggler costs more than a late opening. The same value is surfaced in hints at src/server.ts:325, 442 and 464. Flag: a change would also have to update persistence.ts:77. Q2: Only `bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts` appears more than once in the offlineScripts list (scripts/offline-runner.mjs:64 and :78). No other name repeats (checked with sort | uniq -d over lines 26-182). Q3: src/server.ts:21 `MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000` with the comment "stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)". It is enforced at server.ts:348 (schema max) and server.ts:359 (min with DEFAULT_WAIT_MS, also 55_000 at :20). Verdict: the cap is still justified as a server-side guard for externally connected clients with default ~60s tool timeouts, and its cost is only a re-poll because wait() wakes on events. However, the comment is stale for the hub's own spawned seats: codex-seat.ts:13 sets tool_timeout_sec=120, and seat.ts:417-418 passes a 180_000 ms callTool timeout. The comment should say "external/unconfigured clients" (a recommendation only; no files edited).

challenge.objection: "More seats make it fire less often, not more" overstates it: in a nine-seat working session all seats can be heads-down in tool work at once (no posts), and when the nudge does fire, the post at hub.ts:1057 wakes all nine long-polls (notify at hub.ts:984), so the cost per firing grows with seat count. The verdict still holds because firings are capped (hub.ts:1055), but the clause should say so rather than claim more seats strictly reduce firing.
